data.name: Dinakar
data.gender_notes: Dinakar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Dinakar is derived from two Sanskrit words: ‘Dina’ meaning ‘day’ and ‘Kara’ meaning ‘to do’. Thus, Dinakar translates to ‘God of the day’ or ‘Ruler of the day’. It is believed that this name brings the blessings of the sun god Surya, who is responsible for the cycle of days and the passing of time. The name Dinakar carries the meaning “God of the day” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dinakar usually hope their child will grow to embody god of the day and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Brings the blessings of the sun god Surya.
data.etymology: Dinakar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of the day.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dinakar total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: In Hindu tradition, the sun god Surya is an essential deity, and many rituals and festivals revolve around the worship of the sun. The name Dinakar underscores the importance of the sun god and refers to someone who embodies the sun's energy and power.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Dinakar holds a profound spiritual significance in Hinduism as it is associated with Surya, the sun god. Surya represents power, creativity, and illumination - qualities that help individuals lead a fulfilled and successful life. The name Dinakar signifies the invocation of Surya's blessings for continued growth, enlightenment, and prosperity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Dinakar in Hinduism symbolizes the divine charioteer of the sun god, Surya. It is believed that Dinakar helps guide the sun across the sky each day. The name signifies the inner light that illuminates the spiritual path.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Dinakar was a renowned Jain Tirthankara of the 23rd Tirthankara cycle in Jainism. The name Dinakar carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Jainism is an ancient Indian religion that emphasizes nonviolence, self-control, and renunciation. Tirthankaras are the spiritual teachers who guide the faith.
